title: Job change tracking for sales: How to reconnect with past buyers
summary: Reconnect with past buyers through job change tracking. Get a sales workflow, outreach examples and a template to review contact updates.
body_markdown:
Job change tracking for sales means monitoring when known contacts move to another employer or take a different role. These updates can help sales teams reconnect with former buyers, reassess account fit, and keep customer relationships current.


Before acting on an alert, check the person’s history with your company. A former product administrator knows you differently from someone who attended a demo and decided against buying. Keep that history available so the seller can decide whether there is a reason to talk again.


## Job change tracking and champion tracking


Job change tracking can cover any contact you choose to monitor. Champion tracking focuses on people with a previous relationship to your business, especially those who supported a purchase or helped others use your product.


Someone who worked at a customer company may never have encountered your product. Check what your team knows about their involvement before describing them as a champion.


[UserGems’ tracking documentation](https://help.usergems.com/settings/track-contacts) distinguishes previous opportunity contacts from product administrators and users. It also records the relationship to help determine how a contact should be approached.


Organize your list by the relationship you can support with evidence:


Previous relationship Evidence to look for What to check before reconnecting


Buyer Opportunity records showing their involvement in the purchase Whether their new responsibilities and employer fit your offer


Product administrator or user Account records or a customer team’s confirmation of their product use Their experience with the product and the work they now own


Evaluator Meeting notes or an evaluation record Why the evaluation ended and whether that reason still applies


Employee at a customer company Employment history, with no confirmed product interaction Whether they know your company at all


These suggested categories can overlap. A buyer may also have used the product or advocated for it internally, so keep the underlying notes available.


## How to build a job change tracking workflow


### 1. Start with contacts whose relationship you can explain


Start with your customer and opportunity records. Account managers and customer success colleagues can help confirm who used the product or took part in a purchase.


Record each person’s previous employer and role, then link to the relevant account or opportunity. Explain how they knew your company. A note such as “Administered the product at a customer account” gives the next seller more context than “past champion.”


Read any notes about their experience before suggesting another conversation. The customer team may have recorded unresolved problems or dissatisfaction. Familiarity with the product doesn’t tell you whether the person would recommend it.


Assign someone to maintain the list, review uncertain matches, and remove contacts who no longer belong in the program.


### 2. Choose how you will find job changes


For a small list, manual review may be manageable. You can also use a tool that monitors saved contacts. Whichever method you choose, make sure your team can maintain it and assign follow-up.


[LinkedIn Sales Navigator](https://www.linkedin.com/help/sales-navigator/answer/a10710125) lets you save leads and receive updates, including job changes. Start by finding and saving the relevant person, then review the alerts associated with your saved leads.


[UserGems documents weekly job-change scans](https://help.usergems.com/signals/past-champions) for contacts supplied to its Past Champions signal. When it detects a change, it shows the new company and updated contact information.


Keep the date you observed the update separate from the date the person says they started the role. If you can’t establish the start date, leave it unknown. A profile update you find today may describe an earlier move.


### 3. Verify the person and the move


Before updating records or sending a message, compare the person’s profile with the previous employer and role in your records. If the match is unclear, check other public information or ask the colleague who knows them.


Check what changed too. An internal promotion calls for different follow-up from a move to another company. Someone who adds an advisory position may still work for their existing employer.


Save the source URL and the date you checked it. Put the contact on hold for review if sources disagree about their current role.


### 4. Assess the new employer before planning outreach


Check the new employer against your[ideal customer profile](https://blog.floworks.ai/ideal-customer-profile-template/) . Its business model, size, or location could put it outside the market you can serve, even when you know the contact well.


Read the person’s current responsibilities. If they’ve moved into an unrelated function, there may be little reason to discuss the same product. You’ll also need to confirm budget and purchasing authority; a familiar title won’t establish either.


Check whether the new employer is already a customer or has an active opportunity, and coordinate with its account owner before reaching out. If the person left a current customer, ask the original customer team to check whether it needs a new point of contact there.


Record the decisions for each account separately. The same move can prompt a prospecting review at the new company and a relationship update at the old one.


### 5. Update records and assign the next action


When you record the new employment, preserve the person’s previous relationship with your company. Follow your CRM’s record structure and your team’s rules for company fields. Automatically replacing the old employer could lose context the seller needs.


Make it easy for the seller to find earlier opportunity notes and see which employer they belong to. Record the new company’s status and account owner clearly so the update doesn’t trigger overlapping campaigns.


After reviewing the update, choose a next action:


Decision Suggested condition


Reconnect The move is verified, the previous relationship is understood, and the new account and role are relevant


Research further The identity, relationship, current responsibilities, or account fit still needs checking


Update records only The change is confirmed, but there is no relevant reason for sales outreach


Assign someone to carry out the next action. Mark the alert as reviewed once the decision has been recorded.


## Outreach examples for different previous relationships


These messages are hypothetical examples. Use a relationship description only when your records support it, and adapt the product reference to the person’s current work.


### A former buyer


> Congratulations on the new role. We worked together on your previous team’s purchase, and I wanted to reconnect. Does the work you now own involve a similar need, or has your focus changed?


Ask about their new context before assuming that the previous purchase makes your product relevant there.


### A product administrator or user


> I saw you’ve moved to a new company. You previously worked with our product as an administrator, so I wanted to ask whether similar work is part of your new role. If it is, would a brief catch-up be useful?


Ask the customer team about the person’s experience before using this message. Acknowledge unresolved issues appropriately if there were any, and avoid implying that the experience was positive.


### A previous evaluator


> Congratulations on the move. We spoke during your previous team’s evaluation, although it didn’t lead to a purchase. Are you looking at any similar work in the new role, or is your remit different now?


Read the reason the evaluation ended before sending this. The same objection could still apply, or the contact may prefer to leave the discussion there.


If you only know that someone worked at a customer company, ask whether they encountered your product. Describe the connection as accurately as your records allow.


## A practical example: deciding whether to reconnect


Consider this hypothetical example: a product administrator at an existing customer moves to a manufacturing company.


A customer success colleague confirms the person’s product use and explains their experience. You verify the new role and check that the manufacturing company fits your target market. Because another seller owns the account, you share the previous relationship and the source of the update with them.


That seller reviews the new responsibilities before deciding whether to send a message. Relevant work gives them a reason to ask about the new team’s process. If the person has moved into an unrelated function, the team can update its records and leave the account out of this campaign.


Meanwhile, the original customer team checks who has taken over the administrator’s responsibilities. Both teams can act on the update while leaving the sales opportunity unconfirmed.


## Job change tracking template


Keep the evidence behind each decision in a spreadsheet or CRM view. The seller should be able to review the following information:


Field What to record


Contact Name and profile URL or another identifier that distinguishes the person


Previous relationship Buyer, user, evaluator, or another supported description


Relationship evidence Relevant account notes, opportunity, or confirmation from a colleague


Previous employment Employer and role associated with that relationship


Current employment New employer, role, and the kind of change observed


Timing and source Source URL, date checked, and employment start date if known


Verification Confirmed, uncertain, or awaiting review, with the reason


New-account assessment ICP fit, existing customer or opportunity status, and account owner


Follow-up Assigned seller, next action, and outcome


Set a review schedule your team can maintain. Recheck the current role and account status before outreach when the original observation falls outside the period your process considers recent.


## How to choose job change tracking tools


Choose tools around the work your team needs to do. Reviewing a short contact list may need a different setup from coordinating updates across several account owners.


Approach What it involves What to evaluate


Manual review A team member checks a defined list against current public information Time required, identity checks, and consistent record keeping


Saved-lead alerts A platform surfaces updates for contacts you have saved Relevant alert coverage and how sellers record their decisions


Dedicated contact tracking A product monitors an uploaded or connected contact list Matching quality, refresh frequency, available integrations, and handling of uncertain changes


[Common Room’s job-change playbook](https://www.commonroom.io/playbooks/track-job-changes/) shows how contacts can be imported and filtered for organization changes, with segments and alerts to support follow-up. It also describes filtering by account owner with a CRM connection.


Evaluate a product with a contact list whose history your team understands. Check the results for incorrect matches and missed changes, and review the usable updates. Confirm which features and integrations the proposed plan includes.


## Measure what happens after an alert


Record how many detected changes your team verifies. Check how many new accounts fit your market and whether the reviewed contacts have a previous relationship your records support. Together, these measures show whether the research is usable for sellers.


Record outreach and sales outcomes separately, using consistent definitions for replies, meetings, and qualified opportunities. An updated contact record should remain a different status from a new sales opportunity.


For pipeline reporting, distinguish opportunities created through a reconnect from existing opportunities it helped progress. Counting both as newly sourced pipeline would overstate the program’s contribution.


When comparing results with other prospecting sources, account for differences in prior relationships and account fit. Use a small trial to find workflow problems, and avoid treating it as proof of a conversion advantage.
